title: corydalis racemosa var. setacea
intro: Corydalis racemosa var. setacea, commonly known as Western Poppy or Western Corydalis, is a perennial flowering plant in the Papaveraceae family. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its purported health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antispasmodic, and analgesic properties, which can help relieve pain, anxiety, and insomnia. The bioactive constituents of Corydalis racemosa var. setacea include alkaloids such as demethoxyyangonin and protopine, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including sedation and muscle relaxation. The plant's health benefits are thought to be due to its ability to interact with the body's opioid receptors, providing pain relief and promoting relaxation.
